old_title: Ukraine war live: Trump envoy 'scared' to travel to Kyiv for peace talks
new_title: Ukraine war latest: Putin official warns Trump over peace talks
old_text:
Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff is reportedly "too scared" to travel to Kyiv for peace talks throwing planned negotiations into doubt, according to a report in the Kyiv Independent.
US negotiators are expected to visit Kyiv and Moscow in the coming days as Washington seeks to revive efforts to end Russia's war in Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelensky previously said.
Russia's Tass news agency afterwards said the visit by envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner was supposed to take place on Saturday and Sunday.
The Kyiv visit has now been thrown into doubt amid claims that Witkoff is concerned about Russian warnings that he should not travel the Ukrainian capital, the Kyiv Independent reported.
"The Russians don't want them to come here to Kyiv, and Witkoff is always sensitive to Russian sentiment," a source told the outlet. "They're being told there that it's dangerous."
The pair were due to arrive in Kyiv by plane, with the outlet previously reporting that Witkoff does not like taking the train to Kyiv.
Zelensky previously said it was "very important" that US negotiators continue to be active in peace talks.
Watch: Zelensky says he receives information about first airlines refusing flights to Russia
Kremlin says possibility of Ukraine peace remains but there is no concrete basis
We've heard from Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, who said on Friday that the possibility of a Ukraine peace settlement remained, but that there was no concrete basis for it right now.
He declined to confirm if US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were due to visit Moscow in the coming days.
Asked to comment on reports that the envoys were expected to visit Russia and Ukraine over the weekend for peace negotiations, Peskov said any contacts would be announced when they take place.
WHO warehouse storing Ukrainian medical supplies struck, organisation says
A World Health Organization warehouse storing medical supplies in Ukraine has been struck during an air attack overnight in Kyiv Oblast, the WHO said on Friday.
"Access to the site remains restricted due to heavy smoke and safety concerns, while assessments of possible damage and stock losses are ongoing," WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said.
"No WHO personnel were affected."
Kushner and Witkoff to visit Moscow and Kyiv this weekend - Russian news agency
As we earlier reported, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky said negotiators were expected in Moscow and Kyiv.
We've now heard from Russian news agency Tass, which says negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to visit the two countries on Saturday and Sunday, citing a source.
The pair have spearheaded US efforts to broker a Ukraine peace agreement, but have so far not succeeded.
Air Tanzania suspends flights to Moscow after Zelensky warning
Air Tanzania said it was temporarily suspending flights from Dar es Salaam to Moscow from Friday.
It has become the first airline to take this action after Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky warned this week that the skies over Russia were unsafe.
The airline said on Facebook that it took the step after "a routine risk assessment of the operating environment along the route".
Finland investigating surveillance drone near south coast
Finland has said it is investigating whether a surveillance drone on the shore of its south coast has violated the Nordic country's territory.
An investigation launched by the Border Guard authority seeks to determine where, when and how the aircraft entered Finnish territory and how it possibly crossed Finland's border.
Preliminary examination suggests the aircraft is a Geoscan 701 type drone, which is used by both state and civilian actors.
European country's have repeatedly alleged drone incursions related to the Russia-Ukraine war in the past year, but the Border Guard said it could not confirm the drone's origin, operator or purpose at this stage.
The drone was intended for surveying and mapping and did not pose a danger to the public, the defence ministry said on Wednesday.
Germany once cosied up to Putin. Now they are Russia's public enemy number one in Europe
Eighteen years before Russian tanks rolled into Ukraine, the then German chancellor Gerhard Schröder was asked for his opinion on President Vladimir Putin.
"I am thoroughly convinced that the Russian president wants to transform Russia into a democracy and that he is doing so out of a deeply held conviction," he said in 2004. That same year, Putin was re-elected by a landslide in an election widely regarded as a sham.
His comments underlined a spirit of cooperation and friendship that had grown between the two countries since the end of World War Two. Germany's economy hugely benefited from imports of cheap Russian gas, culminating in the construction of the Nord Stream gas pipeline under the Baltic Sea.
That relationship has now hit an all-time low. On Wednesday, the deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, Dmitry Medvedev, threatened Germany with direct military strikes in response to Berlin's claim that Russia was behind a failed explosive drone attack at Leipzig Airport last month. The drone, which was laden with explosives, failed to detonate near a Ukrainian cargo plane.
Suha Kidwai delves into the relationship between Russia and Germany:
Two police officers killed in Russian attack on Dnipropetrovsk, say Ukrainian authorities
Two police officers have been killed in a Russian attack on the Dnipropetrovsk region, local authorities have said.
Another officer was injured in the drone strike on the Pavlohrad district.
"Two people died . One more person was injured. The enemy attacked 2 districts of the region with drones and artillery more than 10 times," said Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration.
"The enemy targeted the Bohdanivka hromada [administrative area] in the Pavlohrad district.
"A fire broke out and a car was damaged. Two police officers were killed. Another is in hospital in a critical condition."
Russia strikes energy infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, say authorities
Russia attacked energy infrastructure facilities in Ukraine's southern Odesa region overnight, Ukraine's energy ministry said on Friday, warning of possible network restrictions.
Odesa governor Oleh Kiper said earlier that one person had been killed and at least five injured in the attack.
In recent weeks, Russia has been actively attacking the Odesa region, focusing on port and energy infrastructure.
Why has Russia set its sights on Germany?
The motives behind Russia's recent hybrid attacks on Germany are partly strategic, with Moscow seeking to exploit divisions in Germany over continuing support for Kyiv, explains Ian Bond, the deputy director of The Centre for European Reform (CER),
State elections are coming up in Germany where the far-right, pro-Russia party, Alternative for Germany (AfD) are topping the polls.
"With these attacks, it seems like Putin is trying to scare Germans into voting for a party who can show that they won't have a problem with Russia," he said.
Mr Bond said that voters opting for a party sympathetic to the Kremlin was a "puzzle" unique to Germany, that was not replicated in eastern European states.
But Putin's targeting of Germany is not exceptional, cautioned Mr Bond.
Several states and institutions have been subject to the Kremlin's aggression - including Poland and the Baltic states.
"Germany is bearing the brunt of recent attacks, but there is quite a lot of this going on," he said.
"The message of this for the rest of Europe and NATO is that, while Russia may not be strong enough to launch direct attacks, it is doing everything it can to destabilise Europe, and try to scare away support for Ukraine."
Mr Bond warned against potential German appeasement of Putin.
"Each one hopes that if he feeds the crocodile enough, the crocodile will eat him last," Mr Bond quoted. "Here, Putin is hoping that the rest of Europe will believe that if it feeds Ukraine to Russia - it'll be the end of it all."
new_text:
Vladimir Putin's deputy foreign minister has issued a warning to Donald Trump as envoys for the US president are believed to be heading to Moscow for talks to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
"The key question is the extent to which the US administration is prepared to invest in finding a real solution to the current crisis, considering the realities on the ground," Sergei Ryabkov said.
This, Mr Ryabkov sought to claim, was a situation which was not developing in Kyiv's favour, Russian state news agency TASS reported.
Trump's envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, are expected to meet Russian president Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday before travelling to Kyiv on Sunday to meet Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky, according to US officials.
The trip comes as Russia continues its attacks despite Zelensky's offer of a temporary air truce. "There will be no airstrikes from our side, and Russia must reciprocally ensure a period of calm, with no airstrikes on its part for as long as necessary to hold these talks," Zelensky said on Friday.
Russia nevertheless launched overnight strikes on Ukraine, killing four people and injuring five in Kamianske in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, while Russian drones also struck Kyiv.
Russia kills five in Ukraine as US envoys arrive in Moscow
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Saturday for talks aimed at reviving stalled efforts to end Russia's war in Ukraine, as fresh Russian strikes killed five people and wounded five more.
The envoys were met at the airport by Russian negotiator Kirill Dmitriev, Russia's TASS news agency reported. They are expected to meet Vladimir Putin before travelling to Kyiv on Sunday for talks with Volodymyr Zelensky.
Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 167 attack drones and ballistic missiles overnight, including around 80 jet-powered Shahed-type drones.
In the Dnipropetrovsk region, five workers were killed at an industrial facility. Regional official Oleksandr Hanzha described them as "people of peaceful professions" who were "simply working their shift".
Russian strikes also damaged a residential building in Boryspil and hit a shopping centre in Mykolaiv region, where two people were wounded.
Putin official issues warning to Trump
Vladimir Putin's deputy foreign minister has issued a warning to Donald Trump as envoys for the US president are believed to be heading to Moscow for talks to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
"The key question is the extent to which the US administration is prepared to invest in finding a real solution to the current crisis, considering the realities on the ground," Sergei Ryabkov said.
This, Mr Ryabkov sought to claim, was a situation which was not developing in Kyiv's favour, Russian state news agency TASS reported.
The trip comes as Russia continues its attacks despite Zelensky's offer of a temporary air truce.
Four killed, five injured in latest Russian attack on Ukraine
Russia launched fresh attacks across Ukraine on Saturday, killing at least four people and injuring five, as Kyiv called for a temporary air truce ahead of US peace talks.
In Kamianske, Dnipropetrovsk region, a Russian strike hit an industrial facility overnight, killing four people and injuring five, Ukrainska Pravda reported. Three of those wounded were hospitalised, with one in intensive care, according to regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha.
Russian drones also struck the Kyiv region, damaging a nine-storey residential building in Boryspil and starting fires on its roof and in an apartment. Two women were injured and taken to hospital, according to the Kyiv regional authorities.
The attacks came despite Volodymyr Zelensky's proposal for a temporary halt to airstrikes while US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner travel to Moscow and Kyiv.
Plane believed to be carrying US envoys Witkoff and Kushner lands in Moscow
A business jet believed to be carrying US president Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and his son-in-law Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Saturday, Russia's Interfax news agency reported, citing aviation sources.
On Friday, Trump said the envoys were heading abroad to attempt to reach a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine.
Ukraine warns Russia preparing plans for northern offensive
Ukraine says Russia is preparing several possible scenarios for a new offensive in the north, including towards Kyiv and Chernihiv, according to presidential aide Pavlo Palisa.
Palisa told journalists last week that Russian military leadership had been tasked with preparing the plans and that Ukrainian intelligence had verified the information through several sources. "Several options were considered," he said, according to the Kyiv Independent.
However, he added that Ukraine was not currently detecting new Russian offensive groupings in those directions. "Our top priority is to prevent the conditions from emerging that would allow Russia to launch any offensive operations at all," Palisa said.
Ukraine has prepared its own response, Palisa said, including plans to "defend, protect, and counter" any Russian move.
Putin's friends finally tell him the truth: Get out of Ukraine to save yourself
Authoritarian populists like Vladimir Putin know that when fellow anti-democrats start calling them "my friend", the writing may be on the wall.
No wonder the Russian president shifted in his seat and tapped his feet impatiently while his erstwhile buddy, the OG populist and Hindu nationalist, Narendra Modi, gave him a mini-lecture - in public - on how he's got to end his war against Ukraine.
The Russian president didn't like what Narendra Modi told him but India's PM is trying to keep the global gang together, explains world affairs editor Sam Kiley
Kyiv seeks EU help as Ukraine faces €23bn defence gap
Ukraine is facing a €23bn (£19.7bn) funding gap for its defence needs this year, as Kyiv warns it may have to cut non-military spending unless allies provide more support.
President Volodymyr Zelensky has asked the EU to bring forward part of its €90bn (£77.2bn) Ukraine Support Loan, which is divided into €45bn for 2026 and €45bn for 2027. The shortfall is meant to cover weapons purchases, personnel, and social support, including around €6bn (£5.1bn) in advance payments for weapons due to be delivered early next year.
"Frontloading the EU loan is not a silver bullet," Chentsov told Euronews, as Kyiv also seeks support from countries outside the EU.
ICYMI: Trump envoys head to Moscow for Putin peace talks
Donald Trump's special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are travelling to Moscow on Saturday for talks with Vladimir Putin before heading to Kyiv on Sunday to meet Volodymyr Zelensky, in a fresh US push to revive stalled peace efforts.
The pair are due to meet Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday, while Zelensky confirmed their Kyiv visit for Sunday, reported Axios.
Trump said the envoys were taking a proposal to end the war, telling reporters: "We have an idea for peace" and saying there was "a good chance" something could be achieved.
Zelensky has called for a temporary halt to airstrikes during the envoys' mission, saying: "There will be no airstrikes from our side, and Russia should reciprocally ensure a period of calm."
However, Russian attacks continued into Saturday, as a strike on Kamianske in Dnipropetrovsk region killed four people and injured five, while Russian drones also hit the Kyiv region, injuring two women in Boryspil.
This followed Friday's Russian drone strike on the headquarters of Ukraine's Security Service in central Kyiv, which injured 12 people, according to Zelensky.
Russian attacks devastate Ukraine's food distribution network
Russian attacks have destroyed around 90 per cent of the food-logistics infrastructure used by Ukraine's retail chains, according to the country's agriculture minister.
"As of today, roughly speaking, 90 per cent of food logistics for retail chains have been destroyed, but that does not mean Ukrainians will be left without food," Taras Vysotskyi said last week.
Vysotskyi said retailers were switching to alternative arrangements, including direct deliveries by truck, to keep food moving. "There will be no threat of hunger or systemic physical shortages of food," he said.
Ukraine's agriculture ministry said exports in August were running at only about a third of potential volume, while data from Spike Brokers showed total agricultural exports in the first 27 days of August had fallen 47.5 per cent from the equivalent period in July.
Russian general accused of masterminding attack on children's hospital 'shot in head'
A Russian general who was linked with an attack on a children's hospital in Ukraine is seriously injured after being shot in the head, according to reports.
Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich is said to have been shot on Thursday morning in the village of Probuzhdenie near Engels, in Russia's Saratov region.
Independent Russian outlet SotaVision said the attack was the third assassination attempt on Russian officers in the past two weeks.
